questions.question: The Acheulian cultural tradition is primarily identified with which types of advanced and symmetrical stone tools?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cleavers and hand-axes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Acheulian cultural tradition is identified with advanced and symmetrical stone tools such as **cleavers** and **hand-axes**. These tools represent a significant step in human technological evolution.
 
• The Acheulian tools are associated with the **Lower Paleolithic period**, dating back approximately 1.7 million years to 200,000 years ago.
 
• These tools were primarily made using a technique called **bifacial flaking**, where stone tools were shaped on both sides to create sharp edges.
 
• Cleavers and hand-axes were multipurpose tools used for tasks such as cutting, chopping, and scraping, enabling early humans to process food and other materials more effectively.
 
• These tools are found at numerous archaeological sites across Africa, Asia, and Europe, showcasing their wide geographical distribution and significance in early human history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cleavers:**

 
 
• Cleavers are characterized by their **straight cutting edge** and broad blade, making them effective for chopping and slicing.
 
• They were used for processing animal carcasses and other heavy-duty cutting tasks.
 
• Cleavers were crafted from large flakes or cores of stone, and their design reflects the advanced skills of early humans in toolmaking.
 
 
 
• **Hand-axes:**
 
 
• Hand-axes are typically **pear-shaped or oval** tools with a sharp edge all around, used for cutting, scraping, and digging.
 
• They are considered one of the most iconic tools of the Acheulian tradition.
 
• Hand-axes demonstrate early humans’ ability to plan and execute complex designs in toolmaking.
 
 
 
• **Lower Paleolithic Period:**
 
 
• This era marks the earliest phase of human tool use, spanning from approximately 2.5 million years ago to 200,000 years ago.
 
• It witnessed the emergence of Homo erectus, who is believed to have created Acheulian tools.
 
• The Acheulian culture represents an advancement from earlier Oldowan tools, showcasing improved functionality and aesthetics.
 
 
 
• **Global Distribution:**
 
 
• Acheulian tools have been discovered at archaeological sites in countries such as **India, Kenya, South Africa, France, and England**.
 
• Prominent sites in India include **Attirampakkam** in Tamil Nadu and the **Sohan Valley** in Punjab.
 
• The widespread presence of Acheulian tools indicates early human migration and adaptation to diverse environments.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option Analysis:**

 
 
• **Blades and borers:** These tools are associated with the Upper Paleolithic period and are more advanced than Acheulian tools. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
• **Microliths and scrapers:** Microliths are small stone tools from the Mesolithic period, while scrapers were used across multiple periods but are not distinct to the Acheulian culture. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
• **Chisels and adzes:** These tools are typically associated with later Neolithic periods, focusing on woodworking and agriculture. Hence, this option is incorrect.
 
• **Cleavers and hand-axes:** These are iconic tools of the Acheulian tradition, making this the correct option.

questions.question: Which international agreement was signed to control emissions of ozone-depleting substances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Montreal Protocol**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Montreal Protocol** is an international treaty designed to protect the **ozone layer** by phasing out the production and consumption of substances responsible for ozone depletion, such as **chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**, **halons**, and other ozone-depleting substances (ODS).
 
• It was adopted on **September 16, 1987**, and entered into force on **January 1, 1989**, with subsequent amendments strengthening its provisions.
 
• The Protocol has been ratified by **197 countries**, making it one of the most universally supported agreements in history.
 
• It includes legally binding commitments for countries to reduce ODS production and consumption in accordance with specific schedules.
 
• Due to its successful implementation, the Protocol is considered instrumental in reducing the harmful effects on the ozone layer, with predictions of full recovery of the ozone layer by the mid-21st century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Basel Convention:**

 
 
• The **Basel Convention**, adopted in **1989**, deals with the control of transboundary movements of hazardous wastes and their disposal.
 
• Its primary focus is to prevent the dumping of hazardous waste from developed nations into developing countries.
 
• It does not address ozone-depleting substances, making it unrelated to the question.
 
 
 
• **Earth Summit:**
 
 
• The **Earth Summit**, held in **1992** in **Rio de Janeiro**, addressed sustainable development and environmental protection.
 
• Key outcomes included Agenda 21 and the Rio Declaration, focusing broadly on environmental issues rather than ozone depletion specifically.
 
 
 
• **Kyoto Protocol:**
 
 
• The **Kyoto Protocol**, adopted in **1997**, focuses on reducing greenhouse gas emissions to combat climate change.
 
• It is not related to ozone-depleting substances but rather to global warming and carbon emissions.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol's Success:**
 
 
• The Protocol is widely regarded as the most successful environmental treaty due to its universal ratification and effectiveness in reducing ODS emissions.
 
• It has been amended multiple times (London, Copenhagen, Montreal, Beijing amendments) to include new substances and stricter controls.
 
• The **Kigali Amendment** (2016) added hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) to the list of controlled substances due to their high global warming potential.
 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
• **Ozone Layer:** The ozone layer is a vital part of the Earth's atmosphere, located in the stratosphere, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the sun.
 
• **ODS Impact:** Substances like CFCs cause ozone depletion by releasing chlorine and bromine upon breakdown, which react with ozone molecules.
 
• **Montreal Protocol Day:** September 16 is celebrated as **International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer** to commemorate the signing of the Montreal Protocol.
 
• **Scientific Data:** According to reports, the ozone hole over Antarctica has significantly reduced in size since the Protocol's implementation.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes aims to skill rural youth who are poor and provide them with jobs having regular monthly wages or above the minimum wages?

options.text: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana (DDU-GKY)** was launched on **25th September 2014**, under the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), Government of India.
 
• It aims to **skill rural youth aged 15–35 years**, especially those from **economically disadvantaged households**, and provide them with sustainable employment opportunities.
 
• DDU-GKY focuses on **income generation through regular jobs** where wages are above the **minimum wage** threshold.
 
• The scheme targets rural youth from families below the poverty line identified under the **Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC)** data.
 
• It is part of the **National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM)**, aimed at reducing poverty by promoting diversified and gainful employment opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Garib Kalyan Rozgar Yojana (GKRY):**

 
 
• Launched in **June 2020** during the COVID-19 pandemic to provide immediate livelihood opportunities for migrant workers.
 
• Focused on **public infrastructure creation** and rural development by employing returnee migrants.
 
• This scheme aimed to generate **125 days of employment** for migrant workers in **116 districts** across six states.
 
 
 
• **Prime Minister Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP):**
 
 
• Implemented by the **Ministry of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME)** since **2008**.
 
• The scheme focuses on generating employment through **entrepreneurship** and promoting **self-employment ventures** in rural and urban areas.
 
• It provides **financial assistance** for setting up micro-enterprises.
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY):**
 
 
• Launched in **2015** under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE).
 
• Aims to provide **short-term skill training** to youth to make them employable.
 
• Focuses on skill certification and training across various sectors based on industry demands.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of DDU-GKY:**
 
 
• Provides **free skill training** in various sectors like IT, hospitality, healthcare, retail, and construction.
 
• Offers placement-linked training programs ensuring job opportunities for candidates post-training.
 
• Special focus on marginalized groups such as **women, differently-abled, and SC/ST communities**.
 
• Supported by **public-private partnerships** to ensure industry-relevant training.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Eligibility Criteria for DDU-GKY:**

 
 
• Beneficiaries must belong to rural households listed in **SECC 2011**.
 
• Applicants should be aged between **15–35 years**.
 
• Relaxation in age for categories such as **SC/ST, women, and persons with disabilities** is provided.
 
 
 
• **Funding Support:**
 
 
• DDU-GKY is **100% centrally funded**, with funds allocated based on states' rural population and poverty levels.
 
• Training costs, job placement expenses, and accommodation for candidates are covered under the scheme.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• DDU-GKY has successfully skilled and placed thousands of rural youths in diverse industries.
 
• Promotes **economic growth** by reducing poverty and unemployment in rural areas.

questions.question: The Human Genome Project, launched in 1990, had the goal of determining the sequence of how many billion base pairs that make up human DNA?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.0 billion base pairs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Genome Project** (HGP) was an international scientific research project launched in **1990**, aimed at mapping and understanding all the genes in human DNA.
 
• The primary goal of the HGP was to determine the complete sequence of the **3 billion base pairs** that make up human DNA.
 
• DNA is composed of four chemical bases: **adenine (A), thymine (T), cytosine (C), and guanine (G)**, which are paired to form the rungs of the DNA double helix.
 
• The Human Genome Project was completed in **April 2003**, two years earlier than planned.
 
• The completion of the HGP marked a significant milestone in biological sciences, providing valuable insights into genetics, disease, and human evolution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Goals of the Human Genome Project:**

 
 
• To identify all the approximately **20,000-25,000 genes** in human DNA.
 
• To determine the complete sequence of the **3 billion DNA base pairs**.
 
• To store this information in public databases for further research.
 
• To improve tools for data analysis and enable personalized medicine.
 
• To address ethical, legal, and social implications arising from genomic research.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Base Pairs in DNA:**
 
 
• The sequence of base pairs determines the **genetic instructions** for building proteins, which perform essential functions in the body.
 
• The pairing rules are specific: **A pairs with T**, and **C pairs with G**, ensuring accurate replication and functioning of genetic material.
 
 
 
• **Key Achievements of the Human Genome Project:**
 
 
• Discovery of genes associated with diseases like **cancer, Alzheimer’s, and cystic fibrosis**.
 
• Development of **genetic testing** for inherited conditions.
 
• Advancement in **personalized medicine**, allowing treatments tailored to individual genetic profiles.
 
• Increased understanding of **human evolution** and migration patterns through genetic studies.
 
 
 
• **Collaborating Organizations:**
 
 
• The HGP was a collaborative effort involving institutions from the **United States, the United Kingdom, Japan, France, Germany, and China**.
 
• It was coordinated by organizations like the **National Institutes of Health (NIH)** and the **U.S. Department of Energy**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Genome Sequencing:**
 
 
• Used in **identifying genetic disorders** and developing targeted therapies.
 
• Plays a critical role in understanding genetic factors in diseases like diabetes, cancer, and cardiovascular disorders.
 
• Enables advancements in **forensic science**, agriculture, and bioinformatics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Timeline of the Human Genome Project:**

 
 
• Started in **1990** and completed in **April 2003**, ahead of schedule.
 
• Initial funding was provided by the **United States government**, followed by global collaborative investments.
 
 
 
• **Ethical Implications:**
 
 
• Raised concerns about **privacy, genetic discrimination, and ethical use of genetic information**.
 
• Prompted the development of legislation like the **Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act (GINA)** in the U.S.

questions.question: India’s foreign trade structure changed significantly under British rule. During the colonial period, what kind of goods did India primarily export?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raw materials**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under **British colonial rule**, India primarily exported **raw materials** such as cotton, jute, indigo, and tea to Britain and other parts of the world.
 
• India was forced to supply raw materials to fuel the **Industrial Revolution in Britain**, which significantly altered India’s traditional economic structure.
 
• The British policies discouraged **industrialization in India** and promoted India as a source of raw materials and a market for British manufactured goods.
 
• Examples of raw materials exported during this period include **cotton** (to feed British textile mills), **spices**, **opium** (exported to China), and **tea**.
 
• This export-oriented policy led to the de-industrialization of traditional Indian industries like textiles, as they could not compete with cheaper, mass-produced British goods. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Colonial Economic Policies:**

 
 
• The British implemented policies aimed at transforming India into a **supplier of raw materials** and a consumer of British manufactured goods.
 
• Heavy duties were imposed on **Indian manufactured goods**, making them non-competitive in the international market, while raw materials were exported at low costs.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Indian Industries:**
 
 
• Traditional industries such as **textile weaving, handicrafts, and metalwork** suffered greatly due to the influx of British factory-made goods.
 
• India became reliant on British imports, which stifled local entrepreneurship and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Key Raw Materials Exported:**
 
 
• **Cotton:** Exported to British textile mills to produce clothes.
 
• **Jute:** Used in manufacturing gunny bags and other items.
 
• **Indigo:** Vital for dyeing textiles, primarily exported to Europe.
 
• **Opium:** Exported to China, leading to the infamous **Opium Wars** between Britain and China.
 
 
 
• **De-industrialization:**
 
 
• Due to the dominance of British goods and policies, India’s traditional industries declined, leading to **widespread unemployment** and poverty.
 
• The **Indian economy** shifted from being an exporter of manufactured goods to one heavily reliant on agriculture and raw material exports.
 
 
 
• [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
 
• The British East India Company’s control over trade routes facilitated the export of raw materials and the import of British goods.
 
• The introduction of the **railway system** in India was aimed at improving the transportation of raw materials to ports for export.
 
• India’s dependence on agriculture and raw material exports during the colonial period led to frequent famines and economic stagnation.

questions.question: What name did Dobereiner give to his groups of three similar elements?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Triads**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner**, a German chemist, introduced the concept of **triads** in **1829**. He grouped three chemically similar elements together based on their atomic weights and properties.
 
• In a **triad**, the atomic weight of the middle element is approximately the average of the atomic weights of the other two elements. For example, in the triad of lithium (Li), sodium (Na), and potassium (K), the atomic weight of sodium is roughly the average of lithium and potassium.
 
• Dobereiner's **triads** were an early attempt to organize elements systematically, laying the groundwork for the modern periodic table.
 
• This concept demonstrated that there was a relationship between the properties of elements and their atomic weights, and hinted at the periodicity of elements. This was later developed further by Dmitri Mendeleev and other scientists.
 
• Examples of Dobereiner's triads include: **chlorine (Cl), bromine (Br), iodine (I)**, and **calcium (Ca), strontium (Sr), barium (Ba)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Development of the Periodic Table:**

 
 
• The periodic table evolved over several centuries as scientists discovered patterns in the properties of elements.
 
• Early theories included **Dalton's atomic theory**, which provided the foundation for understanding atomic structure.
 
• Dobereiner's triads were one of the first systematic attempts to group elements based on their properties and atomic weights.
 
• Later, **John Newlands** proposed the **Law of Octaves** in 1864, suggesting that every eighth element had similar properties when arranged in increasing atomic weight.
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev** created the first widely accepted periodic table in **1869**, predicting properties of elements yet to be discovered.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Dobereiner's Triads:**
 
 
• Not all elements could be grouped into triads, and many elements did not fit into this pattern.
 
• Dobereiner's triads could only identify relationships between a few elements, leaving many others unaccounted for.
 
• For example, elements like **fluorine** and **oxygen** could not be arranged into triads.
 
 
 
• **Dobereiner's Legacy:**
 
 
• While Dobereiner's triads had limitations, they were an important milestone in the development of the periodic table.
 
• They demonstrated the importance of atomic weight in determining chemical properties.
 
• Dobereiner's work inspired later scientists, such as Mendeleev, who built upon his ideas to create the modern periodic table.
 
 
 
• **Modern Periodic Table:**
 
 
• The modern periodic table is organized by **atomic number** rather than atomic weight, a discovery made by **Henry Moseley** in **1913**.
 
• It consists of **118 confirmed elements**, grouped into periods (rows) and groups (columns) based on their electron configuration and chemical properties.
 
• Elements are categorized into **metals, non-metals, and metalloids**, with further divisions such as alkali metals, transition metals, and noble gases.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner:**

 
 
• Born in **1780** in Germany, Dobereiner was a chemist who contributed significantly to early chemistry.
 
• He discovered **catalytic reactions** and developed the concept of triads.
 
• His invention of the **Dobereiner's lamp**, which used platinum as a catalyst to ignite hydrogen, was one of his noteworthy contributions.
 
 
 
• **Triads in Chemistry:**
 
 
• The concept of triads was based on observing similarities between groups of three elements.
 
• Although limited, the triads demonstrated a fundamental concept that elements could be organized systematically.
 
• This idea contributed to the development of the periodic law and table.

questions.question: What does ‘dyarchy’ mean in the context of the 1919 Act?

options.text: Power to the judiciary and legislature

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dual control in provinces**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **'dyarchy'** refers to a system of **dual governance** introduced by the **Government of India Act, 1919**. This was a significant constitutional reform in British India, aimed at gradually introducing self-governance.
 
• The system divided the subjects of administration into two categories: **Transferred Subjects** and **Reserved Subjects**. This division of powers between the elected Indian ministers and the British officials in the provinces is what is referred to as "dual control."
 
• The **Transferred Subjects** included areas such as education, health, and agriculture, which were to be administered by the Indian ministers accountable to the legislative councils.
 
• The **Reserved Subjects** included areas like law and order, finance, and revenue, which remained under the direct control of the British governors and their executive councils.
 
• The dyarchy system was implemented in the **provincial governments** of British India, marking a step towards **democratic decentralization**. However, it was met with criticism due to the restricted powers given to Indian ministers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government of India Act, 1919:**

 
 
• The Government of India Act, 1919, also known as the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms**, was enacted to increase the participation of Indians in the governance of British India.
 
• It introduced the concept of **dual governance (dyarchy)** at the provincial level.
 
• This act also expanded the participation of Indians in the legislative councils and introduced the system of **bicameralism** at the central level.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Dyarchy:**
 
 
• The dyarchy system failed to provide real power to Indian ministers as the most important subjects like finance, law, and police were reserved for the British governors.
 
• The Indian ministers had limited power, and their decisions could be overruled by the British authorities.
 
• The system was criticized as being complicated and ineffective in addressing the demands of self-rule.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Government of India Act, 1919:**
 
 
• It paved the way for further constitutional reforms, such as the **Government of India Act, 1935**, which introduced provincial autonomy and further expanded the role of Indians in governance.
 
• The Act marked the beginning of the process of **decentralization** in British India, even though it was limited in its scope.
 
 
 
• **Features of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Power to the judiciary and legislature:** This was not a feature of dyarchy but relates to the separation of powers principle in governance.
 
• **Dual monarchy system:** This refers to a political system where two monarchs rule simultaneously, which is unrelated to the Government of India Act, 1919.
 
• **Centralised governance:** This refers to a system where the central authority retains most of the power, which is opposite to the decentralization attempted under the dyarchy system.

questions.question: What is the primary function of the Control Unit within a CPU?

• The **Control Unit (CU)** is a crucial part of the **Central Processing Unit (CPU)**, responsible for managing and coordinating all operations within the CPU.
 
• Its primary function is to **direct the flow of instructions and data**, ensuring proper communication between the memory, input/output devices, and the processor.
 
• The Control Unit deciphers instructions fetched from memory and determines the sequence of operations required for execution. 
 
• It manages **instruction decoding** and ensures that the relevant components of the CPU are activated to perform tasks efficiently.
 
• The Control Unit coordinates the execution of instructions by generating control signals

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of social legislation introduced by the British during the colonial period in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Widow Remarriage Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The Widow Remarriage Act** of **1856** was introduced by the British in India to promote the remarriage of widows.

questions.question: What can be the shape of the trajectory of a charged particle moving in a uniform magnetic field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Helical path**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A charged particle moving in a **uniform magnetic field** experiences a force due to the magnetic field, called the **Lorentz force**.
 
• The Lorentz force acts perpendicular to both the velocity of the particle and the magnetic field, causing the particle to move in a curved path, resulting in a **helical trajectory**.
 
• The shape of the trajectory depends on the initial velocity of the particle relative to the magnetic field:
 
 
• When the velocity is perpendicular to the magnetic field, the particle moves in a **circular path**.
 
• When the velocity has both parallel and perpendicular components to the magnetic field, the result is a **helical path**.
 
 
 
• The radius of the helical path (cyclotron radius) is determined by the equation: **r = mv / (qB)**, where:
 
 
• **m** is the mass of the particle.
 
• **v** is the velocity component perpendicular to the magnetic field.
 
• **q** is the charge of the particle.
 
• **B** is the magnetic field strength.
 
 
 
• The pitch of the helix depends on the component of the velocity parallel to the magnetic field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other types of trajectories:**

 
 
• **Elliptical path:** This occurs in certain non-uniform magnetic fields or when other forces, such as electric fields, act on the particle. However, this is not the case in a uniform magnetic field.
 
• **Parabolic path:** A charged particle follows a parabolic path when it moves under the influence of an electric field only, not when in a uniform magnetic field.
 
• **Hyperbolic path:** A hyperbolic trajectory is related to gravitational interactions or certain scattering phenomena, not applicable to a charged particle in a uniform magnetic field.
 
 
 
• **Applications of the helical motion of charged particles:**
 
 
• **Mass spectrometry:** Helical motion is exploited to separate ions based on their mass-to-charge ratio in a magnetic field.
 
• **Particle accelerators:** Devices like cyclotrons use circular orbits in magnetic fields to accelerate charged particles.
 
• **Auroras:** The beautiful light displays in polar regions are caused by charged particles from the solar wind following the Earth's magnetic field lines in a helical motion.
 
 
 
• **Key equations:**
 
 
• The force on a charged particle in a magnetic field is given by **F = q(v × B)**.
 
• The angular frequency (cyclotron frequency) of the particle is **ω = qB / m**, where **q** is the charge, **B** is the magnetic field strength, and **m** is the mass of the particle.
 
 
 
• The helical motion is a combination of circular motion perpendicular to the magnetic field and linear motion parallel to the field.

• The **Nationwide Mass Drug Administration (MDA) Campaign** for Lymphatic Filariasis (LF) was launched by **Jagat Prakash Nadda**, the then Union Minister of Health and Family Welfare in India.
 
• The campaign is a part of India's commitment to eliminate **Lymphatic Filariasis (LF)** as a public health problem, in line with the global goal of eradicating the disease by **2030**.
 
• The **Mass Drug Administration** involves the distribution of preventive medications, such as **Diethylcarbamazine Citrate (DEC) and Albendazole**, to the population at risk of the disease.

• The disease causes severe swelling in the arms, legs, breasts, and genitalia, leading to disability and social stigma.
 
• Three species of worms are primarily responsible: **Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia malayi, and Brugia timori**.
 
• Lymphatic Filariasis is endemic in more than **70 countries**, with a significant burden in tropical and subtropical regions.
 
 
 
• **India's Efforts to Eliminate Lymphatic Filariasis:**

• During his tenure as Health Minister, he spearheaded several health initiatives, including the **Nationwide Mass Drug Administration Campaign** for Lymphatic Filariasis and the implementation of the **Ayushman Bharat Yojana**.
 
 
 
• **Global Programme to Eliminate Lymphatic Filariasis (GPELF):**
 
 
• The World Health Organization (WHO) launched this program in **2000** to eliminate Lymphatic Filariasis as a public health problem worldwide by **2030**.
 
• The two main strategies of GPELF are **interrupting transmission** through MDA and **managing morbidity and preventing disability** in affected individuals.
 
• It is estimated that around **36 million people** currently suffer from the disfiguring and debilitating effects of LF globally.
